newsitem.title: USA: U.S. cigar imports zoomed 67 pct in 1996 - study.
newsitem.headline: U.S. cigar imports zoomed 67 pct in 1996 - study.

text.p: The cigar smoking trend is showing no signs of slowing yet, with 1996 imports of premium cigars into the United States soaring 67 percent compared with last year.

According to Cigar Aficionado magazine, 293.7 million units were imported in 1996, up 117.4 million from 1995. The increase equals the total number of cigars imported to the United States in 1993 and means the market has nearly tripled in four years.

Cigars have become incrediby popular recently, notably with young professionals and increasingly, women. The craze has put several new companies on Wall Street's map, with initial public offerings by General Cigar Holdings Inc Consolidated Cigar Holdings Inc and Caribbean Cigar Inc.
